pairs.description: Aspirin inhibits platelet aggregation and irritates the gastric mucosa, adding a pharmacodynamic bleeding effect to warfarin anticoagulation; salicylates can also increase free warfarin.
pairs.clinical_significance: Combined anticoagulant and antiplatelet effect is associated with a substantially higher risk of major and gastrointestinal bleeding.
pairs.recommendation: Combination generally avoided unless a specific indication exists (e.g., certain mechanical valves or recent coronary stenting); if used, monitor closely for bleeding and consider gastroprotection.
pairs.source_attribution: Warfarin sodium tablets, FDA label (DailyMed), Section 7 Drug Interactions

pairs.description: NSAIDs inhibit platelet function and injure the GI mucosa; the effects of warfarin and NSAIDs on GI bleeding are synergistic.
pairs.clinical_significance: Users of both drugs have a risk of serious GI bleeding higher than users of either drug alone.
pairs.recommendation: Avoid combination; paracetamol is the usual analgesic alternative. If unavoidable, use lowest dose for shortest time and monitor for bleeding.
pairs.source_attribution: Ibuprofen tablets, FDA label (DailyMed), Drug Interactions / Warnings

pairs.description: Mefenamic acid, like other NSAIDs, impairs platelet function and damages the GI mucosa, adding to warfarin's anticoagulant effect.
pairs.clinical_significance: Synergistic increase in risk of serious gastrointestinal bleeding.
pairs.recommendation: Avoid combination; if unavoidable, monitor INR and for signs of bleeding (label: monitor patients using mefenamic acid with anticoagulants such as warfarin).
pairs.source_attribution: Mefenamic acid capsules, FDA label (DailyMed), Section 7.1 (Table 1)

pairs.description: Clopidogrel inhibits P2Y12-mediated platelet aggregation; combined with warfarin there are independent effects on hemostasis.
pairs.clinical_significance: Coadministration increases the risk of bleeding.
pairs.recommendation: Avoid unless specifically indicated (e.g., limited-duration therapy after coronary stenting in atrial fibrillation); if used, monitor closely for bleeding.
pairs.source_attribution: PLAVIX (clopidogrel), FDA label (DailyMed), Sections 5 and 7

pairs.description: Ciprofloxacin inhibits CYP1A2 and CYP3A4, reducing metabolism of warfarin (R-enantiomer) and increasing its anticoagulant effect.
pairs.clinical_significance: INR elevation and bleeding may occur during and shortly after the antibiotic course.
pairs.recommendation: Monitor prothrombin time/INR frequently during and shortly after coadministration; adjust warfarin dose as needed.
pairs.source_attribution: Ciprofloxacin tablets, FDA label (DailyMed), Boxed Warning, Section 5 and Section 7

pairs.description: Clarithromycin is a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor (listed in the warfarin label), reducing warfarin clearance.
pairs.clinical_significance: Risk of serious hemorrhage and significant elevations in INR and prothrombin time.
pairs.recommendation: Monitor INR frequently when starting or stopping clarithromycin; consider an alternative antibiotic.
pairs.source_attribution: Clarithromycin tablets, FDA label (DailyMed), Warnings and Section 7 Drug Interactions

pairs.description: Rifampicin strongly induces CYP2C9, CYP1A2 and CYP3A4, markedly increasing warfarin metabolism and reducing its anticoagulant effect.
pairs.clinical_significance: Loss of anticoagulation (sub-therapeutic INR) with risk of thrombosis; large warfarin dose increases may be required, with over-anticoagulation after rifampicin is stopped.
pairs.recommendation: Avoid if possible; if unavoidable, perform prothrombin time/INR daily or as frequently as necessary and adjust warfarin dose, including after rifampicin is stopped.
pairs.source_attribution: RIFADIN (rifampin), FDA label (DailyMed), Drug Interactions

pairs.description: Ritonavir can alter warfarin concentrations in either direction (inhibition of CYP3A4 and induction of CYP2C9/CYP1A2).
pairs.clinical_significance: Unpredictable change in INR during and after the 5-day course.
pairs.recommendation: Closely monitor INR if coadministration with warfarin is necessary.
pairs.source_attribution: PAXLOVID (nirmatrelvir; ritonavir), FDA label (DailyMed), Sections 4 and 7 (Table 2)

pairs.description: Omeprazole may alter warfarin metabolism (CYP2C19 inhibition affecting R-warfarin).
pairs.clinical_significance: Increased INR and prothrombin time have been reported in patients receiving PPIs, including omeprazole, with warfarin.
pairs.recommendation: Monitor INR when omeprazole is started or stopped.
pairs.source_attribution: Omeprazole delayed-release capsules, FDA label (DailyMed), Section 7 Drug Interactions

pairs.description: Prednisone is listed as a CYP3A4 inducer in the warfarin label; corticosteroids may also alter warfarin response and increase GI bleeding risk.
pairs.clinical_significance: Variable change in INR with added GI ulceration risk.
pairs.recommendation: Monitor INR when starting, changing dose of, or stopping prednisone.
pairs.source_attribution: Warfarin sodium tablets, FDA label (DailyMed), Section 7 Drug Interactions

pairs.description: Omeprazole inhibits CYP2C19, reducing conversion of clopidogrel to its active metabolite.
pairs.clinical_significance: Significantly reduced antiplatelet activity of clopidogrel, even when doses are given 12 hours apart.
pairs.recommendation: Avoid concomitant use; if a PPI is needed, consider one with less CYP2C19 inhibition (e.g., pantoprazole).
pairs.source_attribution: PLAVIX (clopidogrel), FDA label (DailyMed), Sections 5 and 7

pairs.description: Additive antiplatelet effect (P2Y12 inhibition plus COX-1 inhibition) used deliberately as dual antiplatelet therapy.
pairs.clinical_significance: Recognised combination after acute coronary syndrome or stenting, but bleeding risk is increased compared with either drug alone.
pairs.recommendation: Use for a defined indication and duration; monitor for bleeding and consider gastroprotection in high GI-risk patients.
pairs.source_attribution: PLAVIX (clopidogrel), FDA label (DailyMed), Sections 5 and 7

pairs.description: NSAID-induced mucosal injury and platelet inhibition add to clopidogrel's antiplatelet effect.
pairs.clinical_significance: Coadministration increases the risk of gastrointestinal bleeding.
pairs.recommendation: Avoid regular NSAID use where possible; monitor for GI bleeding.
pairs.source_attribution: PLAVIX (clopidogrel), FDA label (DailyMed), Sections 5 and 7

pairs.description: Ritonavir reduces formation of clopidogrel's active metabolite.
pairs.clinical_significance: Reduced antiplatelet effect, with risk of stent thrombosis or recurrent ischemic events.
pairs.recommendation: Avoid concomitant use with nirmatrelvir/ritonavir.
pairs.source_attribution: PAXLOVID (nirmatrelvir; ritonavir), FDA label (DailyMed), Sections 4 and 7 (Table 2)

pairs.description: Rifampicin strongly induces CYP2C19, increasing clopidogrel active metabolite levels and platelet inhibition.
pairs.clinical_significance: May potentiate the risk of bleeding.
pairs.recommendation: As a precaution, avoid concomitant use of strong CYP2C19 inducers such as rifampicin.
pairs.source_attribution: PLAVIX (clopidogrel), FDA label (DailyMed), Sections 5 and 7

pairs.description: Ritonavir strongly inhibits CYP3A4, increasing atorvastatin exposure.
pairs.clinical_significance: Increased risk of statin-related myopathy/rhabdomyolysis.
pairs.recommendation: Consider temporary discontinuation of atorvastatin during nirmatrelvir/ritonavir treatment.
pairs.source_attribution: PAXLOVID (nirmatrelvir; ritonavir), FDA label (DailyMed), Sections 4 and 7 (Table 2)

pairs.description: CYP3A4 inhibition by ritonavir increases amlodipine concentrations.
pairs.clinical_significance: Risk of hypotension, dizziness and peripheral edema.
pairs.recommendation: A dose decrease may be needed; monitor blood pressure.
pairs.source_attribution: PAXLOVID (nirmatrelvir; ritonavir), FDA label (DailyMed), Sections 4 and 7 (Table 2)

pairs.description: Rifampicin, a strong CYP3A4 inducer, markedly lowers nirmatrelvir and ritonavir concentrations.
pairs.clinical_significance: Potential loss of virologic response and possible resistance.
pairs.recommendation: Coadministration is contraindicated.
pairs.source_attribution: PAXLOVID (nirmatrelvir; ritonavir), FDA label (DailyMed), Sections 4 and 7 (Table 2)

pairs.description: Ritonavir increases clarithromycin concentrations (CYP3A4 inhibition); clarithromycin also inhibits CYP3A4.
pairs.clinical_significance: Increased clarithromycin exposure, including QT-related and GI adverse effects, particularly with renal impairment.
pairs.recommendation: Refer to clarithromycin prescribing information for dose adjustment (reduction in renal impairment); consider an alternative antibiotic.
pairs.source_attribution: PAXLOVID (nirmatrelvir; ritonavir), FDA label (DailyMed), Sections 4 and 7 (Table 2)

pairs.description: Ritonavir inhibits CYP3A4, increasing systemic exposure to budesonide.
pairs.clinical_significance: Risk of Cushing's syndrome and adrenal suppression with corticosteroids whose exposure is significantly increased by strong CYP3A inhibitors (low with a short course).
pairs.recommendation: Monitor; alternative inhaled corticosteroids (e.g., beclomethasone) may be considered, particularly for prolonged coadministration.
pairs.source_attribution: PAXLOVID (nirmatrelvir; ritonavir), FDA label (DailyMed), Sections 4 and 7 (Table 2)

pairs.description: Rifampicin, a strong CYP3A4 inducer, decreases artemether and/or lumefantrine concentrations.
pairs.clinical_significance: Loss of antimalarial efficacy.
pairs.recommendation: Coadministration is contraindicated.
pairs.source_attribution: COARTEM (artemether/lumefantrine), FDA label (DailyMed), Sections 4, 5 and 7

pairs.description: Additive QT-interval prolongation (lumefantrine and macrolide antibiotics).
pairs.clinical_significance: Risk of QT prolongation and ventricular arrhythmia.
pairs.recommendation: Use with caution; consider ECG monitoring and correct electrolytes.
pairs.source_attribution: COARTEM (artemether/lumefantrine), FDA label (DailyMed), Sections 4, 5 and 7

pairs.description: Additive QT-interval prolongation (lumefantrine and fluoroquinolone antibiotics).
pairs.clinical_significance: Risk of QT prolongation and ventricular arrhythmia.
pairs.recommendation: Use with caution; consider ECG monitoring and correct electrolytes.
pairs.source_attribution: COARTEM (artemether/lumefantrine), FDA label (DailyMed), Sections 4, 5 and 7

pairs.description: Clarithromycin inhibits CYP3A4, increasing artemether/lumefantrine concentrations, and independently prolongs the QT interval.
pairs.clinical_significance: Pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic potentiation of QT prolongation.
pairs.recommendation: Avoid combination where possible; if unavoidable, use with caution and ECG monitoring.
pairs.source_attribution: COARTEM (artemether/lumefantrine), FDA label (DailyMed), Sections 4, 5 and 7

pairs.description: Clarithromycin inhibits CYP3A4, increasing atorvastatin exposure.
pairs.clinical_significance: Increased risk of myopathy/rhabdomyolysis.
pairs.recommendation: Do not exceed atorvastatin 20 mg daily during coadministration, or withhold the statin for the antibiotic course.
pairs.source_attribution: Atorvastatin calcium tablets, FDA label (DailyMed), Section 7 Drug Interactions

pairs.description: Clarithromycin inhibits CYP3A4 metabolism of amlodipine.
pairs.clinical_significance: Hypotension and acute kidney injury have been reported with CYP3A4-metabolised calcium channel blockers.
pairs.recommendation: Monitor for hypotension and renal function; consider azithromycin as an alternative macrolide.
pairs.source_attribution: Clarithromycin tablets, FDA label (DailyMed), Warnings and Section 7 Drug Interactions

pairs.description: Rifampicin induces CYP3A4 and inhibits the hepatic uptake transporter OATP1B1 (dual mechanism).
pairs.clinical_significance: Delayed administration of atorvastatin after rifampicin is associated with a significant reduction in atorvastatin concentrations.
pairs.recommendation: Administer atorvastatin and rifampicin simultaneously; monitor lipid response.
pairs.source_attribution: Atorvastatin calcium tablets, FDA label (DailyMed), Section 7 Drug Interactions

pairs.description: Dual blockade of the renin-angiotensin system (ARB plus ACE inhibitor).
pairs.clinical_significance: Increased risks of hypotension, syncope, hyperkalemia and changes in renal function, including acute renal failure, without added benefit in most patients.
pairs.recommendation: Avoid combined use of an ARB and an ACE inhibitor.
pairs.source_attribution: Losartan potassium tablets, FDA label (DailyMed), Section 7 Drug Interactions

pairs.description: Both drugs raise serum potassium (reduced aldosterone effect).
pairs.clinical_significance: Risk of severe hyperkalemia, increased with impaired renal function.
pairs.recommendation: Monitor serum potassium within 1 week of initiation or titration and regularly thereafter; used together in heart failure with monitoring.
pairs.source_attribution: ALDACTONE (spironolactone), FDA label, Sections 5.1 and 7.1

pairs.description: Postmarketing reports suggest azithromycin may potentiate the effect of warfarin; infection and reduced vitamin K intake can also raise INR.
pairs.clinical_significance: Possible INR elevation and bleeding during the antibiotic course.
pairs.recommendation: Carefully monitor prothrombin time/INR during coadministration.
pairs.source_attribution: ZITHROMAX (azithromycin), FDA label (DailyMed), Sections 5.4 and 7.2

pairs.description: Antibiotics may raise INR (altered gut flora vitamin K production, acute illness); INR changes are reported when antibiotic courses are started or stopped.
pairs.clinical_significance: Possible INR elevation and bleeding.
pairs.recommendation: Closely monitor INR when starting or stopping any antibiotic.
pairs.source_attribution: Warfarin sodium tablets, FDA label (DailyMed), Section 7 Drug Interactions

pairs.description: Antibiotics may raise INR (altered gut flora vitamin K production, acute illness); INR changes are reported when antibiotic courses are started or stopped.
pairs.clinical_significance: Possible INR elevation and bleeding.
pairs.recommendation: Closely monitor INR when starting or stopping any antibiotic.
pairs.source_attribution: Warfarin sodium tablets, FDA label (DailyMed), Section 7 Drug Interactions

pairs.description: Antibiotics, including tetracyclines, may enhance warfarin effect (altered vitamin K-producing gut flora, acute illness); INR changes are reported when antibiotic courses are started or stopped.
pairs.clinical_significance: Possible INR elevation and bleeding.
pairs.recommendation: Closely monitor INR when starting or stopping any antibiotic; warfarin dose reduction may be needed.
pairs.source_attribution: Warfarin sodium tablets, FDA label (DailyMed), Section 7 Drug Interactions

pairs.description: Regular paracetamol use (rather than occasional doses) has been associated with a rise in INR; mechanism not fully established.
pairs.clinical_significance: Sustained daily paracetamol may increase INR and bleeding risk, although it remains the preferred analgesic over NSAIDs in anticoagulated patients.
pairs.recommendation: Occasional use acceptable; monitor INR if paracetamol is taken regularly for several days or the dose is changed.
pairs.source_attribution: Acetaminophen 500 mg tablets, OTC Drug Facts label (DailyMed), Warnings

pairs.description: Ibuprofen competitively blocks access of low-dose aspirin to platelet COX-1, which can reduce aspirin's irreversible antiplatelet effect; both also injure the GI mucosa.
pairs.clinical_significance: Possible loss of cardioprotective benefit of aspirin and increased GI bleeding risk.
pairs.recommendation: Concomitant use not generally recommended; if occasional ibuprofen is needed, separate dosing from immediate-release aspirin and prefer paracetamol for regular analgesia.
pairs.source_attribution: Advil Dual Action with Acetaminophen (ibuprofen/acetaminophen), OTC Drug Facts label (DailyMed)

pairs.description: Duplicate NSAID therapy with additive COX inhibition.
pairs.clinical_significance: Increased GI ulceration/bleeding and renal toxicity without added analgesic benefit.
pairs.recommendation: Concomitant use of two NSAIDs is not recommended; use one NSAID at a time.
pairs.source_attribution: Mefenamic acid capsules, FDA label (DailyMed), Section 7.1 (Table 1)

pairs.description: Additive injury to the gastric mucosa (corticosteroid impairs mucosal healing; NSAID inhibits protective prostaglandins).
pairs.clinical_significance: Concomitant oral corticosteroid use is a recognised risk factor for NSAID-associated GI bleeding.
pairs.recommendation: Use lowest effective NSAID dose for shortest time; consider gastroprotection (e.g., a PPI) and monitor for GI bleeding.
pairs.source_attribution: Prednisone tablets, FDA label (DailyMed), Precautions - Drug Interactions

pairs.description: Additive injury to the gastric mucosa (corticosteroid plus NSAID).
pairs.clinical_significance: Increased risk of GI ulceration and bleeding.
pairs.recommendation: Use lowest effective NSAID dose for shortest time; consider gastroprotection and monitor for GI bleeding.
pairs.source_attribution: Prednisone tablets, FDA label (DailyMed), Precautions - Drug Interactions

pairs.description: Additive GI mucosal injury; corticosteroids increase salicylate clearance.
pairs.clinical_significance: Increased GI adverse effects; salicylate levels may fall during steroid therapy and rise (toxicity risk) on steroid withdrawal (mainly relevant to higher aspirin doses).
pairs.recommendation: Monitor for GI bleeding; consider gastroprotection in high-risk patients.
pairs.source_attribution: Prednisone tablets, FDA label (DailyMed), Precautions - Drug Interactions

pairs.description: ACE inhibition lowers aldosterone while spironolactone blocks mineralocorticoid receptors; both retain potassium.
pairs.clinical_significance: Significant increases in serum potassium, especially with renal impairment.
pairs.recommendation: Monitor serum potassium and renal function within 1 week of initiation or titration and regularly thereafter; used together in heart failure with monitoring.
pairs.source_attribution: Enalapril maleate tablets, FDA label (DailyMed), Precautions - Drug Interactions

pairs.description: NSAIDs inhibit renal prostaglandins, opposing ARB effects on blood pressure and reducing glomerular perfusion.
pairs.clinical_significance: Attenuated antihypertensive effect; deterioration of renal function, including acute renal failure, in elderly, volume-depleted or renally impaired patients.
pairs.recommendation: Avoid regular NSAID use where possible; if used, monitor blood pressure and renal function.
pairs.source_attribution: Losartan potassium tablets, FDA label (DailyMed), Section 7 Drug Interactions

pairs.description: NSAIDs inhibit renal prostaglandins, opposing ACE inhibitor effects on blood pressure and glomerular perfusion.
pairs.clinical_significance: Diminished antihypertensive effect; deterioration of renal function, including possible acute renal failure, particularly in elderly or volume-depleted patients.
pairs.recommendation: Avoid regular NSAID use where possible; if used, monitor blood pressure and renal function.
pairs.source_attribution: Enalapril maleate tablets, FDA label (DailyMed), Precautions - Drug Interactions

pairs.description: NSAIDs inhibit renal prostaglandin synthesis, reducing the natriuretic and antihypertensive effects of loop diuretics.
pairs.clinical_significance: Reduced diuretic response (relevant in heart failure) and risk of renal failure.
pairs.recommendation: Observe closely for reduced diuretic effect and signs of renal failure.
pairs.source_attribution: Ibuprofen tablets, FDA label (DailyMed), Drug Interactions / Warnings

pairs.description: NSAIDs reduce the diuretic, natriuretic and antihypertensive effects of thiazides via prostaglandin inhibition.
pairs.clinical_significance: Reduced blood pressure control and risk of renal impairment.
pairs.recommendation: Monitor blood pressure and renal function; prefer paracetamol for regular analgesia.
pairs.source_attribution: HYZAAR (losartan/hydrochlorothiazide), FDA label (DailyMed), Indications and Section 7

pairs.description: NSAIDs reduce renal potassium excretion and renal perfusion; spironolactone retains potassium.
pairs.clinical_significance: Severe hyperkalemia and reduced renal function may occur.
pairs.recommendation: Avoid regular NSAID use where possible; monitor serum potassium and renal function.
pairs.source_attribution: ALDACTONE (spironolactone), FDA label, Sections 5.1 and 7.1

pairs.description: Diuretic-induced volume and sodium depletion activates the renin-angiotensin system, so ACE inhibitor initiation causes a larger fall in blood pressure.
pairs.clinical_significance: Excessive first-dose hypotension; combination may also cause deterioration of renal function.
pairs.recommendation: Start enalapril at a low dose (consider reducing or pausing the diuretic beforehand) and monitor blood pressure and renal function.
pairs.source_attribution: Enalapril maleate tablets, FDA label (DailyMed), Precautions - Drug Interactions

pairs.description: Both drugs increase urinary potassium loss.
pairs.clinical_significance: Additive hypokalemia, with risk of arrhythmia.
pairs.recommendation: Monitor serum potassium; potassium supplementation may be needed.
pairs.source_attribution: LASIX (furosemide), FDA label (DailyMed), Precautions / Drug Interactions

pairs.description: Corticosteroids intensify thiazide-induced electrolyte depletion.
pairs.clinical_significance: Additive hypokalemia; corticosteroids may also raise blood glucose.
pairs.recommendation: Monitor serum potassium.
pairs.source_attribution: Prednisone tablets, FDA label (DailyMed), Precautions - Drug Interactions

pairs.description: Beta-2 agonists shift potassium into cells; loop diuretics increase potassium loss.
pairs.clinical_significance: ECG changes and/or hypokalemia from non-potassium-sparing diuretics can be acutely worsened, especially when beta-agonist doses are exceeded.
pairs.recommendation: Use with caution; monitor serum potassium, particularly with high or frequent salbutamol doses.
pairs.source_attribution: Albuterol sulfate HFA inhalation aerosol, FDA label (DailyMed), Section 7 Drug Interactions

pairs.description: Beta-blockers antagonise the bronchodilator effect of beta-2 agonists; metoprolol is beta-1 selective, but selectivity is dose-dependent.
pairs.clinical_significance: Reduced salbutamol response and possible bronchospasm in patients with asthma.
pairs.recommendation: Beta-blockers are generally avoided in asthma; a cardioselective agent such as metoprolol may be used with caution when there is a compelling indication.
pairs.source_attribution: Albuterol sulfate HFA inhalation aerosol, FDA label (DailyMed), Section 7 Drug Interactions

pairs.description: Beta-blockers antagonise the bronchodilator effect of formoterol.
pairs.clinical_significance: Reduced bronchodilator response and possible severe bronchospasm in patients with asthma.
pairs.recommendation: Patients with asthma should not normally be treated with beta-blockers; if required, use a cardioselective agent with caution.
pairs.source_attribution: SYMBICORT (budesonide/formoterol), FDA label (DailyMed), Sections 5.9 and 7

pairs.description: Clarithromycin, a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor, may inhibit budesonide metabolism and increase its systemic exposure.
pairs.clinical_significance: Increased systemic corticosteroid effects (e.g., adrenal suppression), mainly with prolonged coadministration.
pairs.recommendation: Exercise caution; usually acceptable for a short antibiotic course.
pairs.source_attribution: SYMBICORT (budesonide/formoterol), FDA label (DailyMed), Sections 5.9 and 7

pairs.description: Rifampicin induces CYP2C9 and other enzymes that metabolise sulfonylureas (label names glyburide and glipizide; gliclazide is a CYP2C9 substrate).
pairs.clinical_significance: Reduced sulfonylurea exposure; rifampicin may worsen glucose control.
pairs.recommendation: Monitor blood glucose during and after rifampicin therapy; adjust sulfonylurea dose.
pairs.source_attribution: RIFADIN (rifampin), FDA label (DailyMed), Drug Interactions

pairs.description: Rifampicin strongly induces CYP3A4; the label lists decreased exposure of CYP3A4-metabolised calcium channel blockers (e.g., nifedipine), and amlodipine is a CYP3A4 substrate.
pairs.clinical_significance: Reduced antihypertensive effect.
pairs.recommendation: Monitor blood pressure; dose adjustment or an alternative agent may be needed.
pairs.source_attribution: RIFADIN (rifampin), FDA label (DailyMed), Drug Interactions

pairs.description: Rifampicin induces CYP3A4, enhancing metabolism of prednisolone (the active metabolite of prednisone).
pairs.clinical_significance: Reduced corticosteroid effect.
pairs.recommendation: Corticosteroid dose increase may be needed during rifampicin therapy; monitor clinical response.
pairs.source_attribution: Prednisone tablets, FDA label (DailyMed), Precautions - Drug Interactions

pairs.description: Rifampicin induces CYP3A4, decreasing clarithromycin exposure.
pairs.clinical_significance: Reduced clarithromycin concentrations and possible loss of antibacterial efficacy.
pairs.recommendation: Avoid if possible or monitor clinical response; consider an alternative antibiotic.
pairs.source_attribution: RIFADIN (rifampin), FDA label (DailyMed), Drug Interactions

pairs.description: Both drugs are hepatotoxic; given together, the potential for hepatotoxicity is increased. The combination is used together by design in standard tuberculosis regimens.
pairs.clinical_significance: Recognised first-line tuberculosis combination, with increased risk of drug-induced liver injury.
pairs.recommendation: Monitor for symptoms of hepatitis and check liver function tests (baseline and periodically in at-risk patients).
pairs.source_attribution: RIFADIN (rifampin), FDA label (DailyMed), Drug Interactions

pairs.description: Isoniazid induces CYP2E1, which may increase conversion of paracetamol to its hepatotoxic metabolite (NAPQI).
pairs.clinical_significance: Severe paracetamol toxicity has been reported in a patient receiving isoniazid; additive hepatotoxicity.
pairs.recommendation: Keep paracetamol within recommended dose limits and avoid prolonged high-dose use; monitor liver function.
pairs.source_attribution: Isoniazid tablets, FDA label (DailyMed), Precautions - Drug Interactions

pairs.description: Additive QT-interval prolongation (macrolide plus fluoroquinolone).
pairs.clinical_significance: Increased risk of QT prolongation and torsades de pointes, particularly in elderly patients or with electrolyte disturbance.
pairs.recommendation: Avoid combination where possible; if necessary, correct electrolytes and consider ECG monitoring.
pairs.source_attribution: Ciprofloxacin tablets, FDA label (DailyMed), Boxed Warning, Section 5 and Section 7

pairs.description: Fluoroquinolone tendinopathy risk is increased by concomitant corticosteroids.
pairs.clinical_significance: Increased risk of tendinitis and tendon rupture (boxed warning), especially in patients over 60 years.
pairs.recommendation: Avoid combination where possible; discontinue ciprofloxacin at first sign of tendon pain or inflammation.
pairs.source_attribution: Ciprofloxacin tablets, FDA label (DailyMed), Boxed Warning, Section 5 and Section 7

pairs.description: Fluoroquinolones cause dysglycemia; hypoglycemia has been reported with sulfonylureas.
pairs.clinical_significance: Hypoglycemia, sometimes severe.
pairs.recommendation: Monitor blood glucose closely during coadministration.
pairs.source_attribution: Ciprofloxacin tablets, FDA label (DailyMed), Boxed Warning, Section 5 and Section 7

pairs.description: Clarithromycin coadministered with oral hypoglycemic agents can cause significant hypoglycemia.
pairs.clinical_significance: Risk of significant hypoglycemia.
pairs.recommendation: Monitor blood glucose carefully during the antibiotic course.
pairs.source_attribution: Clarithromycin tablets, FDA label (DailyMed), Warnings and Section 7 Drug Interactions

pairs.description: Corticosteroids raise blood glucose (increased gluconeogenesis, insulin resistance).
pairs.clinical_significance: Loss of glycemic control.
pairs.recommendation: Monitor blood glucose; antidiabetic dose adjustment may be required during and after corticosteroid therapy.
pairs.source_attribution: Metformin hydrochloride tablets, FDA label (DailyMed), Section 7 Drug Interactions

pairs.description: Corticosteroids raise blood glucose, opposing sulfonylurea effect.
pairs.clinical_significance: Loss of glycemic control during steroid therapy; hypoglycemia risk when steroid is tapered if sulfonylurea dose was increased.
pairs.recommendation: Monitor blood glucose; adjust sulfonylurea dose during and after corticosteroid therapy.
pairs.source_attribution: Prednisone tablets, FDA label (DailyMed), Precautions - Drug Interactions

pairs.description: Additive osmotic diuresis and natriuresis.
pairs.clinical_significance: Increased risk of volume depletion and hypotension, especially in elderly patients or those with eGFR below 60.
pairs.recommendation: Assess volume status before starting; consider reducing the loop diuretic dose and monitor for hypotension and renal function.
pairs.source_attribution: FARXIGA (dapagliflozin), FDA label (DailyMed), Sections 5.2 and 5.4

pairs.description: Complementary antihypertensive mechanisms; available as a fixed-dose combination. Losartan also attenuates thiazide-induced hyperuricemia.
pairs.clinical_significance: Recognised combination for hypertension.
pairs.recommendation: Compatible combination; monitor blood pressure, electrolytes and renal function as usual.
pairs.source_attribution: HYZAAR (losartan/hydrochlorothiazide), FDA label (DailyMed), Indications and Section 7

pairs.description: Complementary antihypertensive mechanisms (calcium channel blockade plus angiotensin receptor blockade); no significant pharmacokinetic interaction.
pairs.clinical_significance: Recommended dual combination for hypertension (CCB plus ARB).
pairs.recommendation: Compatible combination; monitor blood pressure.
pairs.source_attribution: 2020 International Society of Hypertension Global Hypertension Practice Guidelines (Hypertension 2020;75:1334-57), Drug treatment

pairs.description: Complementary glucose-lowering mechanisms (reduced hepatic glucose output plus insulin secretion).
pairs.clinical_significance: Recognised combination for type 2 diabetes; adding a sulfonylurea increases hypoglycemia risk.
pairs.recommendation: Compatible combination; monitor for hypoglycemia and consider lower sulfonylurea dose.
pairs.source_attribution: Metformin hydrochloride tablets, FDA label (DailyMed), Section 7 Drug Interactions

pairs.description: Different analgesic mechanisms; available together as a fixed-dose OTC combination.
pairs.clinical_significance: Recognised combination for short-term pain relief.
pairs.recommendation: Compatible combination; keep total daily paracetamol and ibuprofen within recommended limits and avoid other paracetamol-containing products.
pairs.source_attribution: Advil Dual Action with Acetaminophen (ibuprofen/acetaminophen), OTC Drug Facts label (DailyMed)

pairs.description: Complementary glucose-lowering mechanisms; available as a fixed-dose combination.
pairs.clinical_significance: Recognised combination for type 2 diabetes.
pairs.recommendation: Compatible combination; monitor renal function and volume status.
pairs.source_attribution: XIGDUO XR (dapagliflozin/metformin ER), FDA label (DailyMed), Indications

pairs.description: Dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker plus beta-blocker; amlodipine does not add to the AV-nodal effects of beta-blockade (unlike verapamil or diltiazem).
pairs.clinical_significance: Recognised combination in hypertension and angina; additive blood-pressure lowering.
pairs.recommendation: Compatible combination; monitor blood pressure and heart rate.
pairs.source_attribution: Standard co-prescription in hypertension and angina practice (dihydropyridine CCB with a beta-blocker)

rules.name: Triple whammy (RAAS blocker + diuretic + NSAID)
rules.description: An ACE inhibitor or ARB (reduced efferent arteriolar tone), a diuretic (volume depletion) and an NSAID (afferent vasoconstriction from prostaglandin inhibition) together impair renal autoregulation.
rules.clinical_significance: Associated with acute kidney injury, particularly in elderly, volume-depleted or renally impaired patients; the losartan and enalapril labels warn that NSAIDs may cause renal deterioration including acute renal failure in patients on diuretic therapy.
rules.recommendation: Avoid adding an NSAID to a RAAS blocker plus diuretic; use paracetamol for analgesia. If unavoidable, use briefly with monitoring of renal function and potassium.
rules.source_attribution: Losartan potassium tablets FDA label Section 7.3; Enalapril maleate FDA label, Precautions - Drug Interactions

rules.name: RAAS blocker + potassium-sparing diuretic in chronic kidney disease
rules.description: ACE inhibitors/ARBs and spironolactone both reduce renal potassium excretion; impaired renal function further limits potassium elimination.
rules.clinical_significance: Markedly increased risk of severe hyperkalemia; the spironolactone label states patients with renal impairment are at increased risk and ACE inhibitors/ARBs further increase it.
rules.recommendation: Combination is used in heart failure only with close monitoring: check potassium within 1 week of initiation or titration and regularly thereafter; at eGFR 30-50 mL/min/1.73 m2 consider starting spironolactone at 25 mg every other day. Generally avoided when serum potassium exceeds 5.0 mmol/L or eGFR is severely reduced.

rules.name: Anticoagulant + antiplatelet + NSAID
rules.description: Warfarin anticoagulation combined with platelet inhibition and NSAID-related platelet dysfunction and GI mucosal injury.
rules.clinical_significance: Very high risk of major and gastrointestinal bleeding; the warfarin and NSAID labels describe synergistic bleeding risk.
rules.recommendation: Avoid NSAIDs in patients on combined anticoagulant and antiplatelet therapy; use paracetamol for analgesia and consider gastroprotection.
rules.source_attribution: Warfarin sodium FDA label Section 7; PLAVIX FDA label Sections 7.4-7.5; Ibuprofen FDA label Drug Interactions

rules.name: Dual antiplatelet therapy + NSAID
rules.description: Aspirin plus clopidogrel (two distinct antiplatelet agents) combined with an NSAID adds GI mucosal injury and further platelet inhibition; ibuprofen may also blunt aspirin's antiplatelet effect.
rules.clinical_significance: Increased risk of gastrointestinal bleeding in patients on dual antiplatelet therapy (typically after acute coronary syndrome or stenting) and possible loss of aspirin cardioprotection.
rules.recommendation: Avoid NSAIDs during dual antiplatelet therapy; use paracetamol for analgesia and ensure gastroprotection where indicated.
rules.source_attribution: PLAVIX FDA label Section 7.4; Advil Dual Action OTC Drug Facts (aspirin warning)

rules.name: Systemic corticosteroid + NSAID with peptic ulcer disease
rules.description: Systemic glucocorticoids and NSAIDs have additive injurious effects on the gastric mucosa.
rules.clinical_significance: High risk of ulcer complications and GI bleeding in patients with peptic ulcer or previous GI bleed; oral corticosteroid use is a recognised risk factor for NSAID-associated GI bleeding.
rules.recommendation: Avoid NSAIDs in patients with peptic ulcer who are taking systemic corticosteroids; use paracetamol and provide PPI gastroprotection if a steroid is required.
rules.source_attribution: Prednisone tablets FDA label, Precautions - Drug Interactions; Ibuprofen FDA label, GI bleeding warning

rules.name: NSAID + RAAS blocker in chronic kidney disease
rules.description: NSAID-induced afferent arteriolar vasoconstriction combined with ACE inhibitor/ARB efferent vasodilation reduces glomerular filtration in kidneys dependent on prostaglandins.
rules.clinical_significance: Deterioration of renal function, including possible acute renal failure, and hyperkalemia in patients with compromised renal function.
rules.recommendation: Avoid NSAIDs in patients with chronic kidney disease taking an ACE inhibitor or ARB; if unavoidable, use briefly with monitoring of renal function and potassium.
rules.source_attribution: Losartan potassium tablets FDA label Sections 5.3 and 7.3; Enalapril maleate FDA label, Precautions - Drug Interactions

rules.name: RAAS blocker + potassium-sparing diuretic + NSAID
rules.description: Three potassium-retaining drugs (ACE inhibitor/ARB, spironolactone and NSAID) combined with NSAID-related reduction in renal perfusion.
rules.clinical_significance: Risk of severe hyperkalemia and acute kidney injury; the spironolactone label lists ACE inhibitors, ARBs and NSAIDs as drugs that increase potassium.
rules.recommendation: Avoid NSAIDs in patients taking a RAAS blocker with spironolactone; use paracetamol. If unavoidable, monitor potassium and renal function closely.

rules.name: Triple antithrombotic therapy (anticoagulant + two antiplatelets)
rules.description: Warfarin combined with aspirin and clopidogrel produces independent, additive effects on coagulation and platelet function.
rules.clinical_significance: Highest bleeding-risk antithrombotic combination; reserved for limited periods in specific situations (e.g., atrial fibrillation after coronary stenting).
rules.recommendation: Avoid outside a specialist-defined indication; if used, keep duration as short as possible, use gastroprotection and monitor INR and bleeding closely.
rules.source_attribution: PLAVIX FDA label Section 7.5; Warfarin sodium FDA label Section 7

rules.name: Systemic corticosteroid + loop diuretic + beta-2 agonist (hypokalemia)
rules.description: Corticosteroids and loop diuretics increase urinary potassium loss, while beta-2 agonists shift potassium into cells.
rules.clinical_significance: Additive hypokalemia with risk of ECG changes and arrhythmia, e.g., during treatment of an acute asthma or COPD exacerbation in a patient with heart failure.
rules.recommendation: Monitor serum potassium (and ECG where indicated); replace potassium as required.
rules.source_attribution: Prednisone tablets FDA label (potassium-depleting agents); LASIX FDA label (hypokalemia with corticosteroids); Albuterol HFA FDA label Section 7.2
